variables.reason: The problem statement names Ra as the first-order absolute moment of height fluctuations. The retrieved record pq_arithmetic_mean_roughness has canonical_quantity arithmetic mean roughness, symbols Ra / R_a, and definition “Mean absolute deviation of surface height from its mean level,” which is exactly the first-order absolute moment of height fluctuations used in the problem. That KB record explicitly gives si_dimension L (unit: m), so the candidate exponent vector with L = 1 and all other base exponents 0 correctly represents Ra as a length quantity in SI base exponents.

The problem labels kt as peak-to-valley height. The KB entry pq_peak_to_valley_height defines mean peak-to-valley roughness height (symbols include k_t, kt) as a roughness-amplitude measure formed from vertical height differences between peaks and valleys. That definition matches the problem’s kt and the KB entry gives si_dimension L (unit: m), so the candidate vector with L = 1 is correct for kt.

The problem’s k_rms is the root-mean-square height. The KB record pq_rms_roughness_height has canonical_quantity root-mean-square roughness height, symbols k_rms / krms, and definition “Root-mean-square fluctuation of surface height about its mean.” That is the same quantity named in the problem and the KB record lists si_dimension L (unit: m). Therefore the candidate vector (L = 1) correctly represents k_rms as a length.

The problem defines Sk as the third central moment of roughness height fluctuations divided by the cube of their RMS height; that is the standardized third moment (skewness). The KB entry pq_height_skewness has canonical_quantity surface-height skewness with symbols Sk / S_k and definition “Third standardized moment of the surface-height distribution,” and explicitly lists si_dimension 1 (dimensionless). This record therefore directly applies to the problem’s Sk and supports the candidate all-zero exponent vector (dimensionless).

The problem’s Ku is the kurtosis of roughness height fluctuations. The KB entry pq_height_kurtosis defines surface-height kurtosis (symbols Ku / K_u) as the fourth standardized moment and records si_dimension 1 (dimensionless). This is the same statistical moment named in the problem, so the candidate exponent vector of all zeros (dimensionless) is correct for Ku.

ES in the problem is the effective streamwise slope of the roughness. The KB entry pq_effective_surface_slope defines effective surface slope (symbols ES, E_x) as the mean absolute gradient of surface height in a horizontal direction and notes that a surface-height derivative is length divided by length and thus dimensionless. The KB record therefore applies directly and supports the candidate all-zero (dimensionless) exponent vector for ES.

Po is surface porosity in the problem. The KB record pq_porosity defines porosity (symbols Po / P_o / phi_p) as a fraction of void or open area and explicitly lists si_dimension 1 (dimensionless). That KB entry matches the problem’s Po and justifies the candidate exponent vector of all zeros (dimensionless).
